1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 d6 3.Nf3.strategy: Develops the knight and tests e5 at once. Black's d6 already covers it, so there is no gain, but the knight also controls d4 and keeps every set-up open for White. A natural, flexible move that leads to a slow fight for central space.
1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 d6 3.Nf3.name: English Opening: King's English Variation

1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 d6 3.g3.strategy: Prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop, so that it supports the knight's grip on d5. White picks a restrained set-up against Black's solid pawn structure and builds long-term pressure rather than striking immediately.

1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 d6 3.g3 c6.strategy: Covers d5 and b5, so White's pieces lose both outposts, and gives Black a compact trio of pawns on c6, d6 and e5. It is solid but slow: Black spends a move without developing a piece and leaves White the freedom to choose the plan.
1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 d6 3.g3 c6.name: English Opening: King's English Variation, Keres Defence

1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 d6 3.Nf3 Bg4.strategy: Develops the bishop outside the pawn chain and puts pressure on the knight that covers d4. If Black takes on f3, White recaptures with a pawn and has doubled pawns, but also the two bishops and a say over how the position opens.
1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 d6 3.Nf3 Bg4.name: English Opening: King's English Variation, Smyslov Defence
